newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: SOCCER-SPORTING BEAT BENFICA IN DERBY, PORTO AHEAD.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPORTING BEAT BENFICA IN DERBY, PORTO AHEAD.

text.p: Sporting beat perennial rivals Benfica, who were reduced to nine men, 1-0 on Saturday to let reigning champions Porto hold on to their lead in the Portuguese first division.
Porto, who crushed newly-promoted Espinho 5-0 away, top the table with 20 points while the two Lisbon sides share second place one point behind.
Sporting's victory in the Lisbon derby should boost players' morale for the team's UEFA Cup game on Tuesday against French side Metz, who defeated the Portuguese 2-0 in France earlier this month.

Benfica dominated the first half but were thwarted by the efforts of Sporting's Belgian keeper Filip de Wilde who made two excellent saves of shots by Moroccan Tahar Kalej and Benfica's star striker Joao Pinto.
Sporting took control in the second half, scoring in the 51st minute with a header from defender Roberto Severo after a free kick by captain Oceano Cruz from just outside the area.

In the 60th minute Benfica, who meet Lokomotiv Moscow away in the Cup Winners' Cup on Thursday, lost Brazilian midfielder Jamir Gomes after a second bookable offence. Ten minutes from the final whistle Tahar Kalej got his marching orders after a second yellow card.

Porto, the only unbeaten side in the Portuguese first division this season, had Serbian winger Ljubimko Drulovic to thank for the extent of their victory since it was his crosses that ended in four of their goals.

Porto, who only need one point from their Wednesday match against Norway's Rosenborg to secure their place in the European Champions Cup final eight, scored two minutes into the match with a shot from Brazilian Edmilson Pimenta inside the box.
Midfielder Rui Barros was next in the 22nd minute and Brazilian striker Mario Jardel, who has dominated Porto's performances this season, took two in the 73rd and 85th minutes.
Austrian midfielder Arnold Wetl completed the route in the 78th minute.
